assumptions.original: One Euclidean Brownian motion under the sample measure μ, relative to the given filtration. The coordinates in a finite index set J come from this same motion. The sample measure is finite. The horizon T is positive and the filtration satisfies the usual conditions. Each coordinate input is real, progressive, and square integrable on the product of μ and time measure restricted to [0,T]. The input row is fixed across levels and can be unbounded.
assumptions.reconstructed: B starts at zero for every omega, has jointly independent increments over disjoint half-open intervals, every continuous real linear functional ell sends B_t-B_s (s<t) to a centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)||ell||², and paths are continuous mu-a.e. B is strongly adapted to F and B_t-B_s is independent of F_s for s≤t. F is right-continuous and every subset S⊆Omega with mu(S)=0 belongs to F_t for every t≥0. A progressive L² integrand is a real process a(t,omega), strongly progressive for F, for which (omega,t)↦a(t,omega) is in L²(mu⊗lambda_T). No fourth-moment or boundedness assumption on eta is imposed.

conclusion.original: For one fixed row of progressive square-integrable real inputs, form the sum of their completed coordinate Itô integrals. Its dyadic squared-increment sum converges in L¹ to the total pathwise square energy. The signed error is integrable at every level. Formula: \begin{gathered}R_t=\sum_j\int_0^t\eta_j(s)\,dB^j_s,\qquad E=\sum_j\int_0^T\eta_j(t)^2\,dt,\\ \int\left|\sum_i(R_{t_{i+1}}-R_{t_i})^2-E\right|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0.\end{gathered}
conclusion.reconstructed: I_j(a)(t,omega) denotes the specified completed Ito integral driven by the scalar coordinate B^j(t,omega)=(B(t,omega))_j. Its representative is the pointwise limit of chosen elementary stochastic integrals off the null complement of their uniform Cauchy event, and zero on that complement; it is held constant after T. Put t_i^n=iT/2^n and Y(t)=∑_j I_j(eta_j)(t). Define E_n=∑_{i=0}^{2^n-1}(Y(t_{i+1}^n)-Y(t_i^n))²-∑_j∫eta_j(s)²d lambda_T(s). Then E_n is mu-integrable for every n and ∫|E_n|dmu→0 as n→infinity.
